title: Best spritesheet/animation gen?

comments.author: fatboyor
comments.body:
I tried a few options  
**1**. Have gemeini generate the sheet, it failed to capture frame to frame chronological sequence after 4-5 frames  
**2**. I then tried a technique call auto-regression, basically use Nth image as reference and a pose plan to dictates the generation of next image. This is slow, expensive, just a little bit more controllable. I have a google app that does that.   
  
**3**. At last, i tried to generate video and downsample, video generation is very good at capture motion sequence. And you can control resolution, ratio, etc. With a bit of pre, post processing technique, you can get pretty smooth animation for basic moves ( some examples : [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LUCTMTZzzBk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LUCTMTZzzBk) ) , but it still sucks at generating exagerated attack animations ( where the models didn't get to leanr lot about )

Some other folks, train their own LORA. My 2 cents at this stage is, let AI generate good enough animation but not perfect animation, if we decide to invest time in it, we may have to learn the real art tools to polish it. This is also a good development process for game, proof of concept, get feedback, then polish. 

  
With all being said, i think **option 3** is by far the easiest, cheapest way for me, basic animation cost around <0.20$ per sheet with background removed.  we can get pretty clean, usable spritesheet that's 'good enough' for demo. 

I think AI's goal should be around 60% completion/quality-wise, not 100% at this stage, thus i actually start building  [https://dreamdog.ai/](https://dreamdog.ai/) to explore using AI as co-pilot thorugh the game development process.

The work is til being built, I see your post, and decide to publish the sprite generation tool(a sub-tool) early on for free, and get feedback. 

Here is my discord as well: [https://discord.gg/F7WCveut](https://discord.gg/F7WCveut)  
Feel free to DM or chat with me

comments.author: agarlington
comments.body:
autosprite is good for full sheets of animations. and then of course you can do this with other image generation pixel art tools like Retro Diffusion and Pixellab, but that's more hands on for you take into an image editing tool and then make the sprite sheet yourself. 
So to answer your question,.I'm gonna second the autosprite dev and say his tool is pretty solid and cohesive. 
then there is Tools from Spriters Resource that lets you upload images to make a sprite sheet.
